The 17th meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP17) opened on Sunday in Yerevan, the capital of Armenia, with countries set to conduct the first global review of collective progress in implementing the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF).

Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan declared the conference open, calling for countries to translate their commitments into concrete actions and measurable results as the 2030 deadline for the framework's targets approaches.

Astrid Schomaker, executive secretary of the Convention on Biological Diversity, expressed hope that COP17 would demonstrate the multilateralism works and that the international community can fulfill its commitments.

She said the assessment of the KMGBF and countries' national reports would help identify implementation gaps and guide efforts to address them.

Adopted in 2022, the KMGBF aims to halt and reverse biodiversity loss by 2030, with a vision of living in harmony with nature by 2050. The global review will assess progress, identify gaps and help determine priority actions to accelerate implementation.

COP17 will run from October 19 to 30 under the theme "Taking Action for Nature."

candidates.title: Returning samples from a Mars moon: Inside the science of Japan's bold MMX mission
candidates.raw_excerpt: Japan's mission to Mars is one of the most ambitious in spaceflight history. It aims to become the first spacecraft to return to Earth from Mars orbit, carrying with it the first-ever samples from the Red Planet system. The mission, known as Martian Moons eXploration (MMX), is a first-of-its-kind endeavor to study the origin of Mars' moons Phobos and Deimos. The robust undertaking includes a landing on Phobos to collect the samples — which will likely be the first from the Mars system to return to Earth — and a search for evidence that could shed light on events during the formation of the solar system billions of years ago. MMX is scheduled to launch on an H3 rocket from Japan's Tanegashima Space Center on Monday (Oct. 19) at 3:41 p.m. EDT (1941 GMT; 4:41 a.m. local time in Japan, Oct. 20). After a 10-month journey to reach Mars, the spacecraft will spend about three years studying Phobos, deploying a rover and landing to collect its samples. The mission will then shift its focus to Deimos for a series of flybys before departing for Earth in November 2030. If all goes according to plan, the MMX sample-return capsule is scheduled to land in Australia in 2031. The spacecraft The MMX spacecraft is comprised of three main parts, as well as a small rover. After release from its H3 launch vehicle, a propulsion module will provide the boost to put MMX on course for Mars. MMX's main exploration module carries the microwave-size IDEFIX rover and most of the mission's scientific instruments, while the return module houses the sample-return capsule. candidates.raw_excerpt: On Oct. 18, 1963, a cat went to space! Félicette was a French "catstronaut" who became the first and only feline to fly to space. While the U.S. and Soviet Union were busy launching primates, dogs and humans, the French decided to join the space race by launching a cat. Félicette, a stray tuxedo cat from the streets of Paris, was a substitute for another cat named Felix, who somehow escaped on launch day. So Félicette went where no cat had ever gone before. She boarded a French Véronique AG1 rocket and soared 130 miles above the Earth before safely parachuting back down. Luckily Félicette made it home alive and well, unlike many of the other animal astronauts that flew during the space race. Félicette, the first cat to fly into space in October 1963, is seen her carrier pre-flight. (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons ) Why it mattered Félicette survived spaceflight, but was short of this world. She was euthanized two months after her recovery so scientists could study her brain. A second cat was launched by the French on Oct. 24, but its flight did not go so well, veering off course. When the cat was found a day later, it was discovered it have died as a result of the journey. From there on, CERMA (Centre d'Enseignement et de Recherches de Médecine Aéronautique) changed its research to flying monkeys. Félicette may have become a footnote to history had it not been for a crowdfunded effort to raise a statue in her memory nearly 60 years later. The sculpture was unveiled in 2019 at the International Space University in Strasbourg, France. European astronauts Helen Sharman, Paolo Nespoli and Reinhold Ewald were on hand for its reveal. A graphene anti-corrosion coating technology has been deployed at scale on the cross-sea bridge of Xiangshan Port in east China's Zhejiang Province.

Stretching about 8.28 kilometers across the port, the bridge is part of China's first cross-sea suburban railway and currently holds the record for the world's longest-span ballastless-track cable-stayed railway bridge.

Cross-sea bridges are exposed to high salinity, high humidity and intense ultraviolet radiation. These harsh marine conditions pose significant challenges to the structures' weather resistance and corrosion protection, as well as the service life of their protective materials.

The graphene-modified heavy-duty anti-corrosion coatings applied to the Xiangshan Port cross-sea bridge were developed by the Ningbo Institute of Materials Technology and Engineering (NIMTE) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and its incubated enterprise.

The coatings offer sound barrier performance, strong adhesion and high salt-spray resistance, helping mitigate corrosion of the bridge's main steel structures in the harsh marine atmospheric environment.

By doubling the service life of conventional anti-corrosion coatings, the new coatings can substantially cut maintenance costs and safety risks, according to the developer.

The large-scale application is expected to enhance the safety and durability of cross-sea rail infrastructure.

As cybersecurity software company Malwarebytes warns in a new post , AI assistants may fall prey to prompt injection attacks, a type of malicious message in which hackers — or possibly rogue AI agents — include hidden instructions designed to influence the victim’s AI. These instructions are frequently made unreadable by humans by concealing the nefarious text, “while leaving content available for an AI system to process,” Malwarebytes explains. To solve the problem, we can’t simply ask “people to look more carefully at their emails.” Instead, companies must carefully determine how AI assistants crawl through the data and extra relevant information from emails. “The real flaw is that the model can’t tell the difference between text it’s supposed to read and instructions it’s supposed to follow,” AI code review service ShipItClean developer Apollo Raines told Malwarebytes. “Stripping hidden content before it reaches the model is worth doing, and every vendor should do it.” As a result, people who are already wary of suspicious emails should learn to “distrust their AI assistant” as well, according to Raines. That shifting terrain is great for Amazon’s bottom line. The robots help decrease friction across the company’s vast logistics empire, increasing speed and strengthening the company’s bottom line. And by allowing robots to “dictate the pace” of work, as Greenwood put it, Amazon is also loosening its need for human labor, disempowering workers both on an individual basis and in any potential collective bargaining arrangements. Beyond the shop floor, Amazon’s robots also serve as a near-constant source of buzzy PR, as exciting achievements in automation overshadow the more mundane but widespread reality of workplace injuries. candidates.raw_excerpt: On Oct. 17, 2016, Orbital ATK (now Northrop Grumman Space Systems ) returned to flight, successfully launching a cargo shipment to the International Space Station (ISS) after its previous cargo mission failed to launch. The private spaceflight company was contracted by NASA to fly cargo to the ISS, and stakes were high for this launch. Orbital ATK's last attempt nearly two years earlier ended in a catastrophic explosion a few seconds after liftoff. Despite some delays, the newly upgraded Antares rocket flawlessly blasted off into the night sky from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia. Six days later, the Cygnus cargo spacecraft arrived at the ISS to deliver food, supplies and science experiments to the crew. An upgraded Orbital ATK Antares rocket soars into the night sky over NASA's Wallops Flight Facility on Wallops Island, Virginia on Oct. 17, 2016. For its part, NASA contracted with Orbital (today, Northrop Grumman) and SpaceX to fly commercial resupply service missions. Both were needed to keep the U.S. operating segment of the station well supplied and with the science and research materials needed for the crew's work. But to their astonishment, they observed a single emission line emanating from it — twice over a span of just three months. Emission lines are bright, narrow bands of light emitted at a specific wavelength by distant celestial objects and other phenomena. candidates.title: Time's up for the leap second
candidates.raw_excerpt:
The world is about to stop adding leap seconds. 

Under the new system, clocks will be allowed to drift from the Earth's actual rotation by up to an hour before anyone has to step in. This means no more leap seconds – for centuries.

Leap seconds have been added to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) to keep it aligned with Earth's irregular rotation. But these adjustments can disrupt digital systems that rely on continuous, precise timekeeping. Since the practice began, 27 leap seconds have been inserted. In 2012, a leap second reportedly caused outages across more than 2,000 networks worldwide. In 2015, the US Intercontinental Exchange halted trading for more than 60 minutes.

The risk of a negative leap second – removing a second rather than adding one – has also raised concerns, as computer systems have never had to implement one on a global scale.

The reform comes after the 28th General Conference on Weights and Measures (CGPM), held in Versailles, France, adopted a resolution this month to introduce continuous UTC from May 20, 2027.

Sometimes described as a shift from leap seconds to a "leap hour," the change is expected to cut maintenance and testing costs for internet services, cloud computing and financial markets.

For most people, the impact will be negligible. Astronomical observations and other applications that depend on Earth's rotation can keep using data that accounts for the difference between the two time scales.

candidates.title: The Orionid meteor shower peaks next week! Here's what to expect
candidates.raw_excerpt: The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, triggering a spectacular display of shooting stars as Earth plunges through the densest part of the debris trail shed by Halley's Comet. Here's what you need to know. When is the best time to see Orionid shooting stars? Orionid meteors are best spotted between the hours of midnight and dawn on Oct. 22, when 10-20 shooting stars may be seen brightening the night sky each hour under ideal dark-sky. The glare cast by the 74%-lit waxing gibbous moon will hide fainter shooting stars for much of the night. Thankfully, the lunar disk will set a few hours after midnight, leaving a window of beautifully dark sky before dawn in which to enjoy the full majesty of the annual meteor shower. Remember to use a trusted website like Time and Date to discover the exact moment of moonset for your location. Where should I look to see Orionid meteors? Orionid shooting stars will appear to originate from a patch of sky, or radiant, located close to the red giant star Betelgeuse in the constellation Orion , which glistens above the southeastern horizon for stargazers in the U.S. during the early hours of Oct. 22. For the best views look 40-90 degrees away from the radiant, where the glowing trains left in the wake of the fast-moving meteors will be at their longest. Be sure to head away from artificial lights and allow 20-30 minutes for your eyes to fully adapt to the dark for the best What causes the Orionid meteor shower? The Orionid meteor shower is active each year as Earth passes through the stream of debris left behind by Comet 1P/Halley , which was observed by a fleet of spacecraft when it last visited the inner solar system in 1986. Shooting stars become visible when particles of the ancient comet collide with our planet's atmosphere at 147,600 miles per hour (237,539 kilometers per hour), vaporizing in a spectacular display of natural fireworks. candidates.raw_excerpt:
China's permanent representative to the United Nations, Fu Cong, called on Friday for stronger global climate governance and an accelerated green and just transition.

Fu spoke at a high-level meeting titled "A Planet Fit for the Future: Restoring Trust through Climate Action," convened by the president of the UN General Assembly ahead of the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31).

He urged the international community to stand united and accelerate action to achieve balanced, positive and practical outcomes at COP31.

Multilateral cooperation remains the most effective way to address climate challenges, Fu said. He called on countries to maintain their resolve and sustain their efforts to fully and effectively implement the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change and the Paris Agreement.

Fu said countries should pursue a green and just transition along pathways suited to their national circumstances and resources, ensuring a just and orderly process. He urged stronger cooperation on critical minerals to build a fair, open, inclusive and mutually beneficial governance system that promotes environmentally sustainable practices and supports the energy transition.

Fu also called for greater support to strengthen developing countries' capacity for climate action. candidates.title: Whoosh at three: 18 million passengers and a changing Java
candidates.raw_excerpt:
The Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Railway, known as Whoosh, marked three years of operation today, having carried more than 18 million passenger trips since its launch.

The 142.3-kilometer line, which operates at a maximum speed of 350 kilometers per hour, has cut travel time between Jakarta and Bandung from over three hours to 46 minutes.

Over the past three years, Whoosh has operated 58,666 train services and accumulated more than 8.9 million kilometers of safe operation, with an on-time rate of 99.4%, according to China Railway International.

A busier railway

Daily services have increased from 14 trains at launch to 62 during peak periods. Single-day ridership peaked at 26,770. During the 2026 Eid al-Fitr holiday period, Whoosh carried more than 132,000 passengers, up over 10% year on year, making it one of Indonesia's busiest rail corridors.

Passenger services have also expanded. Since the introduction of a frequent traveler card in June 2024, 47,577 cards have been sold, with 3,366 sold in July 2026 alone – a monthly record and a roughly 45% increase year on year. 

The operator has also introduced flexible fares, multi-channel ticketing, and ticket change services. 

For elderly passengers, people with disabilities, and pregnant women, stations are equipped with elevators, tactile paving, accessible restrooms, wider ticket gates, and wheelchair ramps, with 32 priority seats and an accessible restroom on each train. 

More than 25,000 priority passengers have been served.
